issues.description: Predicate `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` intercepts every non-Tab key, breaking popup navigation and dismissal.
issues.detail: When the option is off, any key that isn't Tab — arrow keys, PageUp/PageDown, Escape, Backspace, Ctrl-modifiers — hides the popup and forwards the event to the textedit. The check must be an explicit allowlist of Qt.Key_Return/Qt.Key_Enter, not a denylist around Tab. Without narrowing the predicate, the completion popup becomes unusable when the new option is disabled.

issues.description: No tests cover the new option across Enter/Tab/Arrow with the flag on and off.
issues.detail: This patch changes how Enter and Tab interact with the completion popup — the hottest key path in the editor — and ships zero tests. Add the four obvious cases: option=True/Enter accepts, option=False/Enter dismisses-and-forwards, option=False/Tab still accepts, option=False/Arrow navigates. Prose in the PR description is not a regression suite.

issues.description: `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` should be written `key != Qt.Key_Tab`.
issues.detail: Python precedence makes the expression parse correctly, but every reader has to stop and verify. `key != Qt.Key_Tab` is unambiguous, shorter, and matches the rest of the codebase's style. Small readability fix that removes a stumble in a critical control-flow branch.

issues.description: Accept-key policy is complected with widget hide/forward logic and config lookup inside keyPressEvent.
issues.detail: The decision 'is this key an accept key?' is a pure function of (key, config) but lives braided into the event handler alongside widget state and re-dispatch. Extract a named predicate over a named accept-key set so the policy is testable and the handler reads as mechanism, not policy.

issues.description: Config option name says 'use Enter' but the implementation actually decides which keys accept.
issues.detail: `use_enter_for_completions` is read inside a branch that already matched Return/Enter/Tab and fires for any non-Tab key in that set. The flag is really 'only Tab accepts,' not a fact about Enter. The name/semantics drift will bite when a third accept key is proposed; rename or rescope.

issues.description: get_conf is called on every keystroke instead of being cached on the widget.
issues.detail: The plugin config lookup runs on every keyPressEvent while the popup is visible, though the value cannot change mid-keystroke. Hoist the read to popup-show time or cache on a config-changed signal. Small cost, but it separates read-time from decide-time and makes the popup independently testable.

synthesis.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The intent and config plumbing are fine, but the keyPressEvent predicate is wrong-shape: `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` denylists Tab instead of allowlisting Enter/Return, so every non-Tab key (arrows, Escape, PageUp/Down, modifiers) hides the popup and forwards the event when the option is off. The change ships no tests for a keybinding flip on the editor's hottest key path. Secondary cleanups: rewrite the predicate as `key != X`, extract the accept-key policy as a named pure function, cache the config read, and reconcile the option name with what it actually decides.
